issues.detail: Error scenarios and edge cases like corrupted files, network failures during model downloads, and handling conversion failures are mentioned but lack actionable recovery steps.
Installation and CLI commands assume Unix/Linux shell environment; Windows users must adapt venv activation and path separators; no platform-specific guidance for LibreOffice or CLI usage.

scenarios.name: extract-academic-tables
scenarios.rationale: Response A delivers a complete, working implementation using DocumentConverter, accessing doc.tables, calling export_to_dataframe(), and saving CSV files with descriptive names while reporting table count (missing only section headings detection); Response B merely asks for the file path without implementing any of the required methods or functionality.

scenarios.name: extract-images-from-scans
scenarios.rationale: Response A completely ignores the rubric and suggests generic CLI tools (pdfimages, pdftoppm, convert) instead of the required PdfPipelineOptions API with doc.pictures iteration and get_image().save(). Response B directly implements every rubric requirement: configures PdfPipelineOptions with generate_picture_images=True, iterates through doc.pictures, uses get_image(doc).save() to extract images, and prints figure count with page numbers and captions.

scenarios.name: convert-report-to-markdown
scenarios.rationale: Both responses ask for the missing file and fail to meet the rubric's core requirement of calling markdown export functions or showing output, but Response B provides more technical specificity (names Docling, describes linearization of two-column layout, outlines extraction steps) while Response A remains generic; neither includes page count or detected layout structure since no file exists to process.
